postprocess.title: Post-processes
postprocess.intro: A post-process runs after every scan with the saved file. Scans and watchers each pick exactly one; the default is preselected.
postprocess.name: Name
postprocess.isDefault: Default (preselected for new scans and watchers; at most one)
postprocess.uploadHint: Any executable file: shell, Ruby or Python script (with shebang) or a binary. Uploading replaces the existing file, it is made executable automatically.

help.title: How a post-process is run
help.run: After saving a scan, sarah starts the file of the selected post-process directly (no shell, no arguments). Everything is passed as environment variables:
help.dir: Files and manifest.json live in SARAH_POST_PROCESS_DIR:
help.inherit: The process also inherits sarah's complete environment, so variables from the systemd unit (e.g. PDF_TARGET_DIR) are passed on as well.
help.cwd: The working directory is the post-process directory; relative paths in the script refer to it.
help.exit: An exit code ≠ 0 counts as failure and is shown as a notification. stdout and stderr go to sarah's log (journalctl -u sarah).
help.serial: Post-processes run one after another, never in parallel – handy for scripts that merge pages into one document.
help.deps: Dependencies (img2pdf, ocrmypdf, Ruby gems …) must be checked or bundled by the file itself.
help.path: PATH is the one of the service (under systemd only /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin …), .bashrc and profiles are not read. So call interpreters installed with mise, rbenv etc. by absolute path in the shebang, e.g. #!/usr/bin/env -S /home/<user>/.local/bin/mise exec ruby@3 -- ruby
help.select: Selecting via API: field PostProcess in POST /scan or POST /watch – the process ID, "none" for none, omitted for the default.

env.SARAH_SCAN_FILENAME: File name of the scan, e.g. scan_3_1_20261112_101500.png
env.SARAH_SCAN_SENSOR: Button of the watcher (empty for api)
env.SARAH_SCAN_NEW_DOC: 1 if this scan started a new document, otherwise 0
